episodes.title: Why The Middle Ages Were A Nightmare For Cults
episodes.description:
When we picture medieval Europe, we usually imagine a terrified population trapped in an ultra-strict religious cult. But if you look at the 14th-century records of Montaillou—a tiny mountain village interrogated by an obsessive inquisition—the reality was completely unhinged.

Far from being a tightly controlled fundamentalist compound, everyday villagers were openly arguing that Jesus was conceived like anyone else, claiming heaven is just a good mood, and debating whether the human soul is made of blood, wind, or literally a loaf of bread. With a corrupt priest running a local mafia racket and a shepherd who couldn't decide whether Catholics or Cathar heretics had better vibes, Montaillou shatters almost everything we assume about medieval faith.

In this video, we explore why modern religious fundamentalism requires tools the Middle Ages never had, and why medieval life was actually a total nightmare for cult leaders trying to maintain control.
